To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Shank 1, a protein that has a role in synaptic plasticity, is expressed at cone photoreceptor terminals, but not rod photoreceptor terminals.

Shank 1 is present at photoreceptor synaptic terminals in the outer retina and it co-localizes with the postsynaptic density marker PSD-95, a marker of cones, peanut agglutin and the cone specific marker, glycogen phosphoryl.
Shank 1 is localized at cone pedicles in the outer retina and is absent in mice in which the gene is deleted, indicating a role in cone photoreceptor terminals.

the identification and characterization of proteins involved in the regulation of photoreceptor synaptic function.
the role of Shank 1 in the organization of PSDs at cone photoreceptor terminals in the retina.
the role of Shank 1 in the organization of photoreceptor terminals and how this may be involved in photoreceptor signaling.

Shank 1 expression in cone photoreceptor terminals may play an important role in the organization of synaptic scaffolding at cone terminals.

the Shank family of scaffolding proteins is expressed at cone terminals in the outer retina, and that Shank proteins could have important roles in the organization and function of cone terminals.
